sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the applicant and the informant used to run the company, known to take government contracts and the informant had a separate company in which he was individually a director.

The said company of the applicant and the informant entered into an agreement with the company of the informant that in future, they shall be jointly taking government contracts as partners, as such, the applicant, who happens to be the director of the company, is stated to have usurped the amount due towards the informant which emanated out of the said agreement entered into between the parties.

RIVAL CONTENTIONS:
Arguments on behalf of Applicant:
5.
Learned Senior Counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has the apprehension of his arrest.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
The case of civil nature has been converted to criminal one.
It is stated that the applicant is simply a director in the said company and all the said FIRs have been instituted by one and the same complainant.

Learned Senior Counsel has next stated that as the anticipatory bail application of the co-accused persons were rejected by this Court but the co-accused person Sandeep Kumar Garg approached the Apex Court, whereby he was granted anticipatory bail and he has co-operated in trial, he is also entitled for bail on ground of parity.

6. Learned Senior Counsel has also placed reliance on the order of the Apex Court in Sandeep Kumar Garg vs. State of U.P. & Another1, which reads hereinunder:-
"Leave granted.

entities.text: Sandeep Kumar Garg vs. State of U.P. & Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Perused the report submitted by the Medical Board constituted in terms of the earlier order of this Court.
The report records that the appellant is undergoing chemotherapy.
It is stated in the report that he has a tumor in his brain and the Medical Board has in fact recorded that his disease is incurable.
It is also recorded that even if the appellant undergoes surgery, there is every possibility of the disease recurring again.
The charge-sheet has been filed and cognizance has been taken.

Hence, considering the health condition of the appellant, we direct that the appellant shall not be arrested in connection with First Information Report/Case No. 128 of 2018, registered at Police Station - Swarup Nagar, District - Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, subject to the condition that the appellant shall always cooperate for early disposal of the case.

entities.text: Police Station - Swarup Nagar, District - Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The appeal is, accordingly, allowed."
7. Learned Senior Counsel has further stated that the case of the applicant is at a better footing to that of the co-accused persons, as such, he is entitled for anticipatory bail.

Learned Senior Counsel Romendra Mehta vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40229610/
2 has next stated that the companies entered into shareholders' agreement in furtherance of agreement dated 30.9.2013.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Clause 26 provides that if Rajeev Talreja fails to provide bank guarantees, his right in such contract would relinquish.
The informant did not comply with the said Clause 26, although he insisted to get his share in the profit.
8. Learned Senior Counsel has further stated that it is the first informant and not the applicant, who has misappropriated funds.
The informant has participated in the arbitration proceedings and the arbitral award was passed on 15.8.2018.
The said order was set aside on 1.6.2023 and the appeal is pending in this Court as ARPL Nos. 692 of 2023 and 693 of 2023.
The informant had instituted the complaint case no. 1 of 2008 on the same issue as that of arbitration and instituted the instant FIR also.

The applicant was summoned by the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 9, Kanpur Nagar vide order dated 19.2.2019 but the proceedings were stayed by this Court vide order dated 7.9.2021 passed in Application U/S 482 Cr.P.C. No. 11879 of 2021.

entities.text: Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 9, Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The EOW had filed a closure report in the said case in the absence of adequate evidence and subsequently, the protest petition was filed by the informant.
The court concerned rejected the closure report and summoned the applicants u/s 406, 420, 120-B IPC.

Both the parties, the informant and the applicant challenged the stay order dated 29.10.2021 and the revision of the informant was allowed vide order dated 15.3.2022, as such, the petition U/S 482 Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant was dismissed as infructuous.
The said order is not on merits.
The no dues certificate has been issued by the Bank.

9. Learned Senior Counsel has further stated that the FIR is delayed by 5 years and it has been lodged to settle personal vendetta of business rivalry with an intention to harass the applicant and extort money.
The tender work has already been completed by the company.

The criminal history of the applicants stands explained, as is evident from Annexure-13 filed in the supplementary affidavit dated 27.8.2023, which categorically states that as the work of SPBL Energy Private Limited,
Kanpur, was completed, nothing remains there between the parties, as such, the FIR shall be withdrawn as such.

Arguments on behalf of Informant:
10. Per contra, learned Senior Counsel for the informant has stated that the criminal history of the applicant company has not been properly explained.

The non-bailable warrants have been issued against the applicant Romendra Mehta by the Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 10, Kanpur Nagar and the instant anticipatory bail application was filed subsequent to it.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail as the anticipatory bail application of the co-accused persons Sandeep Kumar Garg and Gaurang Garg has already been rejected by this Court on 18.7.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. 7760 of 2023.

11. Learned Senior Counsel has further argued that the case of the applicant is covered by the judgement of the Apex Court passed in Shivam Vs. State of U.P. and Another2, and he has pointed out the relevant para-43(8) and (10) of the said judgement, which reads hereinunder:-
"44(8).

Where the accused is avoiding appearance before the Court after the cognizance of offence has been taken by the Court on a police report or in a complaint and coercive processes have been repeatedly issued against him and there is no valid explanation given by the accused for his non-appearance before the Court.
12. Learned counsel has also placed reliance on the judgement passed in Sabir Ali vs. State of U.P.3.

entities.text: Sabir Ali vs. State of U.P.3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant in collusion with the other co-accused persons forged the bank money worth Rs. 11.55 crores and used the same as genuine in Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited.
There is ample evidence on record against the applicant.

Learned Senior Counsel has stated that the co-accused person Sandeep Kumar Garg has been granted protection by the Supreme Court and the case of the applicant is not at par with the co-accused persons, as such, the anticipatory bail application cannot be allowed by this Court.

13. Learned Senior Counsel for the informant has further stated that the Apex court has granted bail to the co-accused persons Sandeep Kumar Garg on the basis of his health condition, as such, it is not a case of parity.
The said order is not on merits of the case, but on the poor health condition.

Rather,
it is the case of parity of rejection of the bail of the co-accused person of this Court.

CONCLUSION:
14. In Ramesh Bhavan Rathod vs. Vishanbhai Hirabhai Makwana (Koli) and another4, paragraphs 25 and 26 reads as under:-
25.

entities.text: Ramesh Bhavan Rathod vs. Vishanbhai Hirabhai Makwana (Koli)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We are constrained to observe that the orders passed by the High Court granting bail fail to pass muster under the law.
They are oblivious to, and innocent of, the nature and gravity of the alleged offences and to the severity of the punishment in the event of conviction.

In Neeru Yadav v. State of U.P., (2014) 16 SCC 508, this Court has held that while applying the principle of parity, the High Court cannot exercise its powers in a capricious manner and has to consider the totality of circumstances before granting bail.

entities.text: Neeru Yadav v. State of U.P., (2014) 16 SCC 508
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court observed:
"17.

Coming to the case at hand, it is found that when a stand was taken that the 2nd Respondent was a history sheeter, it was imperative on the part of the High Court to scrutinize every aspect and not capriciously record that the 2nd Respondent is entitled to be admitted to bail on the ground of parity.
It can be stated with absolute certitude that it was not a case of parity and, therefore, the impugned order clearly exposes the non-application of mind.
That apart, as a matter of fact it has been brought on record that the 2nd Respondent has been charge sheeted in respect of number of other heinous offences.
The High Court has failed to take note of the same.
Therefore, the order has to pave the path of extinction, for its approval by this Court would tantamount to travesty of justice, and accordingly we set it aside."

sentences.text: Another aspect of the case which needs emphasis is the manner in which the High Court has applied the principle of parity.
By its two orders both dated 21 December 2020, the High Court granted bail to Pravin Koli (A-10) and Kheta Parbat Koli (A-15).

Parity was sought with Sidhdhrajsinh Bhagubha Vaghela (A-13) to whom bail was granted on 22 October 2020 on the ground (as the High Court recorded) that he was "assigned similar role of armed with stick (sic)".

Again, bail was granted to Vanraj Koli (A-16) on the ground that he was armed with a wooden stick and on the ground that Pravin (A-10), Kheta (A-15) and Sidhdhrajsinh (A-13) who were armed with sticks had been granted bail.
The High Court has evidently misunderstood the central aspect of what is meant by parity.
Parity while granting bail must focus upon role of the accused.

Merely observing that another accused who was granted bail was armed with a similar weapon is not sufficient to determine whether a case for the grant of bail on the basis of parity has been established.
In deciding the aspect of parity, the role attached to the accused, their position in relation to the incident and to the victims is of utmost importance.
The High Court has proceeded on the basis of parity on a simplistic assessment as noted above, which again cannot pass muster under the law.

15. It is true that the case of the applicant and the co-accused person, who has been granted bail by the Apex Court lay at par but in light of the aforesaid judgement in Ramesh Bhavan Rathod (supra),
it stands distinguished on the ground that the co-accused person has been granted bail by the Supreme Court on the ground of his poor health condition, and there is no such ground to grant bail to the applicant.
16.

In Satpal Singh vs. State of Punjab5, the Supreme Court has held that the satisfaction of the court for granting protection under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is different from the one under Section 439 Cr.P.C. while considering regular bail.

entities.text: Satpal Singh vs. State of Punjab5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Pratibha Manchanda and another Vs. State of Haryana and another6, the Apex Court has opined that the relief of anticipatory bail is aimed at safeguarding individual rights.

entities.text: Pratibha Manchanda and another Vs. State of Haryana and another6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While it serves as a crucial tool to prevent the misuse of the power of arrest and protects innocent individuals from harassment, it also presents challenges in maintaining a delicate balance between individual rights and the interests of justice.
The tight rope we must walk lies in striking a balance between safeguarding individual rights and protecting public interest.

17. In view of the above, the present anticipatory bail application is found devoid of merits and is,
accordingly, rejected.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of anticipatory bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case.
